decisions.what_changed: The part's heading (h1) takes focus on the first question of a part and on every screen that is not a question (Up next, block, break offer, break, end), as before. On a later question of the same part focus goes to the question's own labelled region: a div.item-region (role=group, aria-label "Question N", tabindex -1, so a script target and not a tab stop) that SessionScreen now wraps around the question screen: the "cannot be shown" panel, the (possibly parked) renderer wrapper, the confidence slider and the report-a-problem control. The region is a real block box (the old .stage-host stays display: contents inside it) and is never inside a hidden subtree, so focus is not lost when a later question turns out not to be drawable. New src/session/question-focus.ts: QuestionFocus.enter(screenKey, {phase, segmentIndex, problem}) decides 'heading' | 'item' | 'none' once per screen key (same key, same answer: the confidence slider is the same screen as its question) and numbers the questions of a part from 1; itemRegionName(n) is the one place the region's name is made. Screen.svelte gets a focusId prop: focus goes to that element when it is inside the screen and takes focus, else to the heading; the scroll-to-top frame (UX-001) and the tab title (UX-006) are unchanged and run for both targets. Timed blocks, the block keys and render/common/focus.ts are untouched (a block is a non-question screen: heading as before). Focus order: Tab from the heading or from the region reaches the answer field in one press (measured: every counted question of a whole keyboard session on Chromium and WebKit, 1 Tab each), so the number of Tabs per question is what it was; what changes is what a screen-reader user hears (a numbered group per question, the part's name once).

deviations: The region's name is 'Question N' (N = the question's place among those shown in the part), as the task text suggests ('e.g. the question number'). Finding SR-06 asked for a cue 'without an item count (progress is time, DESIGN section 10)'. N is spoken only to screen-reader users and has no total, but if the owner prefers no number, itemRegionName in question-focus.ts is the single place to change (e.g. 'Next question'); the DOM, unit and e2e tests name the number and would need the same edit.

The wait between two questions of a served part ('loading', no error) takes no focus of its own, and a failed wait takes the heading: the task text says every non-question screen keeps the heading, but a served part would otherwise read the part's name again at every wait, which is the repetition D21 is about. For this the loading screen's key is now 'loading' or 'loading:problem' (the failed state remounts the screen so its heading takes focus). The first wait of a part (nothing of it shown yet) still takes the heading.
Practice (PracticeScreen.svelte, not part of this package) still re-focuses its heading for each of its four practice questions; D21 speaks of the counted questions of a part. See requests.

D21 option B does not reduce Tab presses (KBD-12's '96 of 165 Tabs'): from the region one Tab still reaches the field. It removes the repeated part name for screen-reader users. Focusing the field directly (KBD-12's other suggestion) was not asked for.
open_issues: Safari with a mouse: after a click on 'Start' (the previous screen's button, removed from the page) WebKit started Tab from before the header on the first question of a part (3 Alt+Tab presses to the field instead of 1) while a later question's region and a keyboard-only start (the three parts with questions in the whole keyboard session on WebKit) took 1. This is the heading's behaviour as before (not changed here); uxdec-screen.spec.ts therefore starts the part by keys in the Tab-count test.
No focus ring is drawn on the region (outline none, like the h1): it marks where the reader is, not a control. e2e/keyboard.ts focusIsOnPlainTarget already exempts a tabindex -1 container.

decisions.what_changed: One primary action per screen. (1) FocusPicker's 'Start a 20-minute focus session' is a plain hb-btn (type submit unchanged), on the results and on the returning person's ready screen. (2) The Skip and Finish confirm panels of the running session are built with primary="no": 'Keep going' comes first and is the only primary, the skip or finish is the plain button; Escape still means 'Keep going' (ConfirmPanel's existing keydown handler, same as the leave panel of UX-005b; no code change in ConfirmPanel.svelte, its header comment now names the three users). (3) ResultsTalk's copy button lost both 'primary' and 'hb-primary' (now plain hb-btn). The leave panel and the after-save download are as they were, and so is the 'cannot be shown' panel's own primary (Skip), since that question has no other way on.
